title: Everyday light (sample website)
description: A made-up website for testing the app. Short notes about light in daily life.

discover_cards.title: White light holds every color
discover_cards.front: A prism bends each color by a different amount, so white light fans out into a band.
discover_cards.media_alt: A white strip above a band of colors running from red through green and blue to violet.

discover_cards.title: Why the sky is blue
discover_cards.front: Air scatters blue light much more than red light, so blue reaches your eyes from every part of the sky.

discover_cards.title: Why sunsets are red
discover_cards.front: At sunset light crosses much more air, so most blue is scattered away and reds are left.

discover_cards.title: Seeing in the dark
discover_cards.front: Eyes need about 20 to 30 minutes to adjust fully to darkness.
discover_cards.back: One look at a bright screen resets part of that.

discover_cards.title: Carrots and night vision
discover_cards.front: Eating lots of carrots lets you see in the dark.
discover_cards.back: Carrots help only if you lack vitamin A; extra carrots do not add night vision.

discover_cards.title: How fast is light?
discover_cards.front: Light travels about 300,000 km every second: around the Earth seven times.

discover_cards.title: Look up
discover_cards.front: Every color you see is light that something did not keep.
discover_cards.speaker: Theo Placeholder

discover_cards.title: The order of a rainbow
discover_cards.front: A rainbow always shows red on the outside and violet on the inside.

practice_cards.prompt: Put the rainbow colors in order, from the outside in.

choices: Air scatters blue light the most
